title: Duplicate cleanup
prompt: Customer C-0033 wrote in twice about changing their billing address, so we have two tickets for the same thing. Merge the newer one into the older one, then let the customer know with a message they can see.

calls.args: {"operation_id":"comments_add_reply","params":{"ticket_id":"T-2003","body":"Hello, we received your request about updating your billing address more than once,…

agent_text.text: Older is T-2003, newer T-2004. Merge T-2004 into T-2003.

I merged T-2004 (the newer ticket) into T-2003 (the older one), and posted a public reply on T-2003 telling the customer about it.

- **Merge:** the merge call returned T-2003 as the surviving ticket, still open. I didn't re-fetch T-2004 afterwards, so I haven't confirmed it now shows as closed with `merged_into_id` set. The merge response also showed `merged_into_id: null`, but that field belongs to the duplicate, not T-2003.
- **Customer message:** comment CM-06788 is public. It says the duplicate requests were combined into one ticket, that they don't need to do anything, and that we'll update them here.

The two tickets were linked to different orders (T-2003 to O-1126, T-2004 to O-0530). T-2003 keeps O-1126, so whoever handles it may want to check whether O-0530 matters for the invoices.
